claim: v3 detecting-insults with haiku on 8 roles + sonnet ONLY on aggregator does NOT fix the malformed-submission failure mode that X202 (haiku-everywhere) exhibited. Same failure: aggregator runs to completion at $0.68, pipeline_terminal=completed, but submission.csv lacks the 'Comment' column required by the mlebench grader. Medal=none (invalid_submission). Total $3.98 vs X202 $3.80 — sonnet aggregator added only $0.27 of cost vs haiku aggregator, and bought NO bridge across the schema gate. The schema-correctness gate is therefore UPSTREAM of aggregator — likely designer (chooses data layout) or coder (writes inference.py + submission code).

support.grader_error: Submission should have an Comment column

scope: Single Phase 2 run. Refutes the X209 hypothesis that aggregator is the role gating submission shape. Conjoint with E010 (X202 haiku-everywhere also invalid_submission): aggregator-on-sonnet alone does not save it.

vs_x202.verdict: Sonnet aggregator did not change the outcome. Two consecutive haiku-driven detecting runs produce the same malformed submission, suggesting the bug is deterministic given haiku on the upstream schema-defining roles. Designer (writes id_convention.md + data shape) and coder (writes inference.py that builds submission.csv) are the remaining candidates.

limitations: Did not yet test designer-on-sonnet (X217 candidate) or coder-on-sonnet (X218 candidate) to localize the schema bridge.

implications.schema_gate_localization: Aggregator is NOT the bridge. Designer and coder are the next candidates. Designer writes id_convention.md (defines columns) and is the more likely culprit, since the failure is a column-name shape problem.
follow_up_experiments: X217: haiku-everywhere except designer=sonnet (probe designer as the schema gate)
X218: haiku-everywhere except coder=sonnet (probe coder as the schema gate)
X219: sonnet-everywhere on detecting (re-attempt the X201 hypothesis — splitter may have stabilized in main)
